spans.s:
दिदित्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, = दित्सु, ready or wishing to
give away; (an irregular form with double redupli-
cation.)

दिदम्भिषु दिदम्भिषु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. the
Desid. of rt. दम्भ्), intending or wishing to de-
ceive; [cf. धिप्सु and दिप्सु.]

दिदिवि दिदिवि, इस्, इ, m. n. heaven, the sky.
See दीदिवि.
दिदीवि दिदीवि, इस्, m. boiled rice.

दिदृक्षमाण दिदृक्षमाण, अस्, आ, अम् (fr.
the Desid. of rt. 1. दृश्), wishing to see.

दिदृक्षा, f. desire of seeing, wish to see.
—दि-
दृक्षा-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having a desire to see.

दिदृक्षु, उस्, उस्, उ, desirous of seeing (with
acc.); wishing or desiring to examine, desirous of
inspecting.

दिदृक्षेण्य or दिदृक्षेय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
what one likes or wishes to see, conspicuous, at-
tracting.

दिदेविषत् दिदेविषत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत् (fr. the
Desid. of rt. 2. दिव्), wishing to play or sport.

दिद्दा दिद्दा, f., N. of a princess of Kaś-
mīra.
—दिद्दा-क्षेम, अस्, m. ‘having affection for
Diddā,’ an epithet of Kṣema-gupta.
—दिद्दा-पाल,
अस्, m., N. of a man.
—दिद्दा-पुर, अम्, n., N.
of a town built by Diddā.
—दिद्दा-स्वामिन्, ई, m.,
N. of a temple built by Diddā.

दिद्यु दिद्यु, उस्, m. (fr. 2. दिव् or 2. दी or
1. द्यु ?), Ved. a missile weapon, arrow; (Sāy.) a
shining weapon; the sky, heaven.

दिद्युत्, त्, f., Ved. an arrow, a missile (especially
the missiles of the gods and the thunderbolt of Indra);
N. of an Apsaras; (त्, त्, त्), shining, blazing, bright,
(in this last sense derived by some fr. rt. 3. द्युत्.)

दिद्योतिषु दिद्योतिषु, उस्, उस्, उ (fr. the
Desid. of rt. 3. द्युत्), wishing to shine.

दीदि, इस्, इस्, इ, or दीदी, ईस्, ईस्, इ, shining.
—दीद्य्-
अग्नी, m. du., Ved. (according to Sāy.) ‘having
bright fires,’ ‘bright with sacrificial fires,’ epithet of
the Aśvins.
दीदी दीदी or दीदि. See rt. 2. दी, p. 415.
दीदिति, इस्, f. splendor, brightness; [cf. सु-द्˚.]
